key_insight: Routine clinical data collected during TB treatment improves prediction of end-of-therapy status more than it predicts who will relapse after cure.
clinical_relevance: For phase 3 TB trial settings, month-by-month clinical variables can help stratify post-treatment risk, but they are not strong enough on their own to reliably identify future relapse.
method: Harmonised data from 2 Phase 3 TB trials (2,918 participants).
Trained time-resolved models at monthly intervals from baseline through treatment end.
Compared tabular models with large language model-derived embeddings and longitudinal/sparse-variable approaches.
evidence_signal: EOT prediction rose after month 3 to ROC-AUC 0.84, while relapse prediction in patients with favourable EOT outcomes peaked only modestly at ROC-AUC 0.58-0.63 and then declined.
watch_item: Relapse models showed limited performance and lower interpretability when using more flexible or longitudinal representations, so they are not ready to replace relapse-specific biomarkers.
paper_title: Time-resolved predictability of end-of-therapy outcome and relapse after cure in Phase 3 tuberculosis trials
